title: IL HB3851: SCH CD-CYBER-BULLYING

obligations: Create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying, filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
Include procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying staff email and phone and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3))
Include procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved within 24 hours after administration is made aware, and discussing services (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4))

Include procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports, making all reasonable efforts to complete investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying principal, and providing parents information and opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(5))

Include interventions, statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, consistency, and reporting all instances to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(6)-(13))

Include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within permissible scope of jurisdiction and require providing victim with information about available services (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
Make school personnel available for help or to make a report known to parents, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
Every 2 years, review and re-evaluate the policy and make necessary revisions; file updated policy with State Board by September 30 of the subject year (Sec. 27-23.7(d))

Collect, maintain, and submit to State Board non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying; annual report due August 15 each year starting 2024-2025 through 2030-2031 (Sec. 27-23.7(f))

State Board of Education must monitor and provide technical support, review filed policies to ensure requirements, post template by January 1, 2024, adopt rules for data submission and notification, provide data to parents on request, and adopt rules for handling data and privacy (Sec. 27-23.7(d), (f), (g), (h))
State Board may provide grants subject to appropriation (Sec. 27-23.7(j))
prohibitions: Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of these characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a))

No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or vehicles, at designated bus stops, or at school-sponsored or sanctioned events; through transmission from school computer, network, or equipment; or through transmission from nonschool computer if it causes substantial disruption and school administrator or teacher receives a report (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4))
Reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying is prohibited (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7))
False accusation of bullying as a means of retaliation or bullying has consequences and appropriate remedial actions (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(8))
Cyber-bullying includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Passed 2025-08-15. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Amends the Illinois School Code bullying prevention section to prohibit bullying including cyber bullying, adds unauthorized digital replicas to the definition of cyber bullying starting with the 2026-2027 school year, requires schools to create and file bullying prevention policies, collect and report data, and provides for State Board oversight and grants.

Who it applies to

  • School districts
  • Charter schools
  • Non-public, non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools

Effective date

July 1, 2026 (Sec. 99); the unauthorized digital replica addition to cyber-bullying applies beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Bullying: includes cyber-bullying and means any severe or pervasive physical or verbal act or conduct, including communications made in writing or electronically, directed toward a student or students that has or can be reasonably predicted to have the effect of one or more of: placing the student or students in reasonable fear of harm to person or property; causing a substantially detrimental effect on physical or mental health; substantially interfering with academic performance; or substantially interfering with ability to participate in or benefit from services, activities, or privileges provided by a school (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Cyber-bullying: bullying through the use of technology or any electronic communication, including transfer of signs, signals, writing, images, sounds, data, or intelligence by wire, radio, electromagnetic, photoelectronic, or photooptical system, including email, Internet communications, instant messages, or facsimile; includes creation of a webpage or weblog assuming identity of another or knowing impersonation if it creates bullying effects; includes distribution by electronic means to more than one person or posting on an electronic medium accessible by one or more if it creates bullying effects; beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, also includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Digital replica: has the meaning given to that term in the Digital Voice and Likeness Protection Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Policy on bullying: a bullying prevention policy that meets criteria (1) through (13) in subsection (b), including the bullying definition, statement contrary to State law, reporting procedures, parent notification within 24 hours, investigation within 10 school days, interventions, prohibition on retaliation, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, consistency, and reporting all instances to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Restorative measures: a continuum of school-based alternatives to exclusionary discipline that are adapted to needs, contribute to school safety, protect learning climate, teach skills, build relationships, reduce future disruption, and increase accountability if incident is based on religion, race, ethnicity, or other category in Illinois Human Rights Act (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • School personnel: persons employed by, on contract with, or who volunteer in a school district, charter school, or non-public non-sectarian elementary or secondary school, including administrators, teachers, social workers, counselors, psychologists, nurses, cafeteria workers, custodians, bus drivers, school resource officers, and security guards (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Unauthorized digital replica: the use of a digital replica of an individual without the consent of the depicted individual (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Obligations

  • Create, maintain, and implement a policy on bullying, filed with the State Board of Education, based on the State Board template and including the criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Include procedures for promptly reporting bullying, including identifying staff email and phone and a procedure for anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3))
  • Include procedures for informing parents or guardians of all students involved within 24 hours after administration is made aware, and discussing services (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4))
  • Include procedures for promptly investigating and addressing reports, making all reasonable efforts to complete investigation within 10 school days, involving appropriate support personnel, notifying principal, and providing parents information and opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(5))
  • Include interventions, statement prohibiting reprisal or retaliation, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, posting and distribution, evaluation process, consistency, and reporting all instances to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(6)-(13))
  • Include a process to investigate whether a reported act of bullying is within permissible scope of jurisdiction and require providing victim with information about available services (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Make school personnel available for help or to make a report known to parents, students, and school personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Every 2 years, review and re-evaluate the policy and make necessary revisions; file updated policy with State Board by September 30 of the subject year (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Collect, maintain, and submit to State Board non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying; annual report due August 15 each year starting 2024-2025 through 2030-2031 (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • State Board of Education must monitor and provide technical support, review filed policies to ensure requirements, post template by January 1, 2024, adopt rules for data submission and notification, provide data to parents on request, and adopt rules for handling data and privacy (Sec. 27-23.7(d), (f), (g), (h))
  • State Board may provide grants subject to appropriation (Sec. 27-23.7(j))

Prohibitions

  • Bullying on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, religion, sex, national origin, ancestry, physical appearance, socioeconomic status, academic status, pregnancy, parenting status, homelessness, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, military status, sexual orientation, gender-related identity or expression, unfavorable discharge from military service, association with a person or group with one or more of these characteristics, or any other distinguishing characteristic is prohibited in all school districts, charter schools, and non-public non-sectarian elementary and secondary schools (Sec. 27-23.7(a))
  • No student shall be subjected to bullying during any school-sponsored education program or activity; while in school, on school property, on school buses or vehicles, at designated bus stops, or at school-sponsored or sanctioned events; through transmission from school computer, network, or equipment; or through transmission from nonschool computer if it causes substantial disruption and school administrator or teacher receives a report (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(1)-(4))
  • Reprisal or retaliation against any person who reports an act of bullying is prohibited (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(7))
  • False accusation of bullying as a means of retaliation or bullying has consequences and appropriate remedial actions (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(8))
  • Cyber-bullying includes posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means if it creates bullying effects, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b))

Penalties and enforcement

The State Board of Education monitors implementation, reviews filed policies, and if a school fails to file by September 30, sends a written request; if the school fails within 14 days, the State Board publishes notice of non-compliance on its website (Sec. 27-23.7(d)). Schools not in compliance with data reporting under subsection (f) are not eligible for grants from the Illinois Bullying and Cyberbullying Prevention Fund (Sec. 27-23.7(j)). This Section does not prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e)). No new private right of action or criminal penalty is stated in this Section.

How it affects AI deployment

  • If an organization deploys AI that can create digital replicas of individuals, any posting or distribution of an unauthorized digital replica by electronic means that creates bullying effects will be treated as cyber-bullying beginning with the 2026-2027 school year (Sec. 27-23.7(b))
  • Schools must include this in their bullying prevention policy, investigate reports, notify parents within 24 hours, complete investigation within 10 school days, and report data to State Board (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4)-(5), (d), (f))
  • Failure to file or update policy can result in public notice of non-compliance and ineligibility for grants (Sec. 27-23.7(d), (j))
  • The law does not require schools to monitor nonschool-related activity unless a report is received (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4))
  • Free expression and religious exercise protections remain (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5))

Notable exemptions

  • Nothing infringes upon right to free expression or free exercise of religion protected under First Amendment or Illinois Constitution (Sec. 27-23.7(a-5))
  • Item (4) of subsection (a) applies only when a school administrator or teacher receives a report and does not require district or school to staff or monitor any nonschool-related activity, function, or program (Sec. 27-23.7(a)(4))
  • This Section shall not be interpreted to prevent a victim from seeking redress under any other available civil or criminal law (Sec. 27-23.7(e))
  • Subsection (c) is blank (Sec. 27-23.7(c))

Compliance steps

  • Review and update bullying prevention policy to include cyber-bullying, including unauthorized digital replicas, and ensure it meets all 13 criteria in the definition of policy on bullying (Sec. 27-23.7(b), (d))
  • Base policy on State Board of Education template and file with State Board of Education by September 30 of subject year, and every 2 years after review (Sec. 27-23.7(d), (h))
  • Post policy on publicly accessible website, include in student handbook, post where other policies are posted, distribute annually to parents, guardians, students, and personnel including new hires (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(10))
  • Establish procedures for prompt reporting, including identifying staff email and phone, and anonymous reporting (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(3))
  • Establish procedures to notify parents or guardians of all students involved within 24 hours after administration is made aware, and discuss services (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(4))
  • Establish investigation procedures: make all reasonable efforts to complete within 10 school days, involve appropriate support personnel, notify principal, provide parents information and opportunity to meet (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(5))
  • Include interventions, prohibition on retaliation, consequences for false accusations, stakeholder engagement, evaluation process, and reporting all instances to parents (Sec. 27-23.7(b)(6)-(9), (13))
  • Include process to investigate whether reported act is within permissible scope of jurisdiction and provide victim with information about available services (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Make school personnel available for help or to make a report known to parents, students, and personnel (Sec. 27-23.7(d))
  • Collect, maintain, and submit non-identifiable data regarding verified allegations of bullying to State Board annually by August 15, starting 2024-2025 through 2030-2031 (Sec. 27-23.7(f))
  • Ensure compliance with data reporting to remain eligible for grants (Sec. 27-23.7(j))
